children: The lubricant maker plans to enter liquid storage and terminal logistics through a minority stake that will give it management control of Incubit Pipavav Terminal

GP Petroleums Limited has approved a proposed investment of Rs 44.27 crore in Incubit Pipavav Terminal Private Limited (IPTPL), marking its entry into the liquid-storage and terminal logistics business.

The investment will give GP Petroleums a minority equity stake along with management control of the company, subject to definitive agreements and the fulfilment of closing conditions. IPTPL operates a terminal at Pipavav Port in Gujarat.

The move will expand GP Petroleums’ business beyond lubricants and give it a presence in port-based storage and handling. The company plans to explore ways to connect the terminal with markets in the hinterland and assess opportunities to expand operations at Pipavav.
Investment To Be Funded Through Internal Reserves

GP Petroleums will acquire shares from existing IPTPL shareholders, potentially in multiple tranches over one year. The investment will be funded through the company’s internal reserves, while the final consideration may change depending on the valuation of IPTPL’s shares.
The transaction is subject to applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, along with the fulfilment or waiver of conditions precedent.

Ayush Goel, Chairman and Managing Director of GP Petroleums, said the investment would be the first step towards building a logistics infrastructure business alongside the company’s existing lubricant operations.
He said the company aims to generate recurring income from storage and terminal operations, which could help diversify its revenue streams and strengthen cash flows over time.

GP Petroleums manufactures and markets industrial and automotive lubricants, process oils, greases and specialty products under the IPOL brand. The company has more than five decades of industry presence.

The Pipavav investment would give it an opportunity to participate in terminal logistics, where port infrastructure supports the movement and storage of liquid products. GP Petroleums also plans to evaluate other opportunities in logistics infrastructure, with a focus on investment discipline and long-term returns.
